mechaber/part-001.txt.1:main: The measure of a kezayit — some say it is like half an egg. {Rama: And one should eat it together at once, not little by little. And for vegetables one must compress the air space between the leaves, and one measures the kezayit by the vegetables themselves, not the air between them.}

baer-heitev/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) Like half. Magen Avraham ruled it is slightly less than half an egg — see there; likewise Peri Chadash ruled. And see in Kaf HaChayyim and at the end of responsum Chut HaShani: one should be uncertain if one had only slightly less than a kezayit of maror and soaked it in water and it swelled to a kezayit, whether he fulfills with that kezayit on Yom Tov or not. See Yad Ephraim.
baer-heitev/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) In the air. The same applies if there is a hollow in matzah — it does not combine, per the end of Okatzin. Magen Avraham.

beer-hagolah/part-001.txt.1:_: Beit Yosef from the words of Tosafot Chullin 102.

beur-hagra/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) And one should eat it — as written above siman 475 seif 1.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.1:ג: (ג) And regarding vegetables etc. As Tosafot wrote in Yoma 79a s.v. kotevet in the name of Yerushalmi, one must compress its hollow; and as written in ch. 2 of Okatzin regarding onion layers etc., if they have a hollow etc., like sponge cake etc. — see there. And there regarding veal meat etc. But in Menachot 54 we conclude that veal meat that swelled is d'rabbanan, and so Rambam ruled in ch. 4 of Hilchot Avot HaTumah and in ch. 14 of Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot. And at first glance it appears to me that what Ravva said there is a variant reading to avoid difficulty on R. Elazar; but for the conclusion, since R. Elazar's view was accepted in the rejection there, one need not force and say d'rabbanan, and also to say there is no hatara in prohibitions. And in the first chapter of Hametzui it was raised as a question whether there is hatara or not; and although Kesef Mishneh in the name of R' Yitzchak was strained, and Tosafot's difficulty in Menachot there s.v. demei'ikara is also resolved, and also at first glance the sugya in several places that there is hatara in ch. 3 of Taharot regarding gravy etc. — see there. But Rosh and Ra'avad wrote in ch. 3 of Taharot mishnah 4 that there is no hatara, and they adopted the tradents literally; and also Ramban and Rashba in the first chapter of Hametzui strained to resolve Tosafot's difficulty in Menachot cited above and did not reject that halacha — I have no ability to be lenient against them in practice.
beur-hagra/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) Seif 61: the measure of a kezayit etc. It depends on the view of Tosafot and Rambam regarding eruv. For Rambam ruled in Hilchot Eruvin 1:9 that the measure of an eruv is two meals, which are eighteen dried figs, and they are like six eggs; and this is like RiBBa in Eruvin ch. 2 p. 2 and as the Gemara concludes there "half for the shopkeeper." His proof is because the stam mishnah at the end of Peah is like RiBBa, for there it teaches "one does not give less" etc. from a loaf etc., and it is two meals as explained in the mishnah "eight: one who has food for two meals" etc. Tosafot there ch. 2 s.v. agav ruled like R. Shimon, and they bring proof for their words because the sugya of the Gemara everywhere is like him, for it says "like an egg for impurity" etc. — see there. It is not proof, for Rambam explains what is written everywhere "like an egg for impurity" etc. means without its shell, and do not say literally half of half, as written ch. 3 seif 1 that their measures are not equal to each other. Accordingly it is wondrous what Tosafot explained like R. Shimon would be against the stam of ch. 2 of Peah cited above that follows RiBBa as explained. It appears the stam of Peah is no proof for Rambam; on the contrary, from there is proof for Tosafot who ruled like R. Shimon, for at first glance one could say there, in the mishnah's wording R. Shimon "two handfuls" etc. — why not teach its measure explicitly as a loaf of five eggs and a third? Rather the truth in this appears that the measure of "two handfuls" that R. Shimon says is not the measure of two meals for everyone, but the loaf itself is the d'oraisa measure for an infected house, because it is written "and one who eats in the house" etc., and we require a measure of eating, and half the loaf is the measure of one meal — and this is the "peres" mentioned everywhere, namely a peres of the loaf which altogether is two meals. Only in Eruvin they all intended to be lenient, therefore R. Shimon says two handfuls from it are two meals; likewise Rashi there ch. 2 p. 2 s.v. chatziah even though in the measure etc. — see there. And this is what "chatziah for the infected house" etc. means — why did it not teach its measure explicitly as explained; therefore it says chatziah etc., meaning the essence of its measure is chatziah for the house etc. With this the mishnah's wording in ch. 17 of Kelim is settled, where RiBBa precedes R. Shimon — because here it needed to teach chatziah etc. to reveal that the essence of the loaf's measure is for the infected house, and in Eruvin R. Shimon was lenient, and because of this it used the wording of two handfuls as explained; therefore RiBBa precedes R. Shimon so one should not err and say this chatziah etc. refers to RiBBa alone — if it were taught for RiBBa it would be at the end. (Unlike ch. 17 of Kelim where the mishnah's dispute is not taught there, only incidentally; therefore it did not need to teach again this chatziah etc., and therefore there R. Shimon precedes RiBBa and it is taught with R. Yosi in his dispute.) With this the view of Tur siman 399 who wrote that the measure of two meals is eight eggs is settled — it would be wondrous that they ruled not like whom, and see what is written. But accordingly it is fit: their view that they ruled like R. Yehoshua, who learns from Sifra Parah where he says there "one who eats in the house" ten peres from three kav — he holds like R. Shimon regarding an infected house that half a loaf is one meal, only R. Shimon was lenient for eruv and required only two handfuls as explained; and R. Yehoshua holds that always a peres is half that loaf. And so it appears to them in Tur, since R. Yehoshua states it there stam and we do not hear him in Eruvin to be lenient — if so it is eight eggs as explained. Now at first glance one could say in the sugya of Eruvin there where it says the difficulty of R. Chiya against R. Chiya etc. — what he gave etc. — why does it challenge R. Chiya against R. Chiya? Say the first answer of R. Chiya returns because of the difficulty "still for the master nine" etc., and teach "take from them half" like everywhere; and what does it teach with these two changes that where he gives wood he deducts only a third and where he does not give etc. The matter in this appears that R. Chiya first said the first answer "take from them a third," because the contradiction of these two mishnayot at the end of Peah there was difficult for him, as Yerushalmi challenged there: here you say one does not reduce for the poor at the threshing floor, and there you say one does not reduce for a poor man passing from place to place — meaning since it teaches from a loaf for a pundion, which is half a kav as explained from four se'ah for a sela, for grain not needing baking expense one should give more; and it answers: R. Chiya said take from them a third for going out — meaning what is written from a loaf for a pundion is half a kav less a third, for the shopkeeper profits on baking expense, for since half a kav of wheat is sold for a pundion, when the shopkeeper sells the loaf he deducts his expense; accordingly what is written for grain, half a kav is truly a third more than the measure of a loaf for that pundion — and this is R. Chiya's first answer literally; and that it does not teach "take from them half" is because R. Chiya ruled like R. Shimon and explains the stam of Peah cited above according to R. Shimon, therefore it teaches take from them a third — for accordingly two-thirds of half a kav, the measure of that loaf, are eight eggs, and it is literally like R. Shimon; but afterward it was still difficult for R. Chiya from the baraita that teaches "and close" etc. that is not resolved in the first answer take from them a third, as they challenged in the Gemara there "still for the master nine" etc., and it teaches take from them half — accordingly the Gemara sugya there is fit: at first they wanted to resolve that baraita in the first answer, and because of the Gemara's difficulty "still" etc. it resolved in the second answer take from them half. And it properly challenges these two changes of R. Chiya against each other, and teaches "what he gave" etc. — meaning when he gives to a poor man he need not account for wood expense, therefore they measured there with that loaf for a pundion; and in such a case where the master gives wood he deducts only a third, and where he does not give etc. Accordingly the stam of Peah cited above follows R. Shimon, and R. Chiya holds like him, and so R. Chiya in Yerushalmi — therefore he answered take from them a third as explained to establish that stam like R. Shimon, as written in the Gemara "what he gave" etc.; therefore Tosafot properly ruled like R. Shimon. What Rambam brought as proof from the Gemara's wording there "the Sages — RiBBa" etc., implying halacha is like RiBBa — does not decide against Tosafot, because the stam of Peah is like R. Shimon and halacha follows stam mishnah, as explained. But still uncertain from what is written in Eruvin ch. 2: it teaches that two meals etc., and for RiBBa it is dried figs a third of an egg, and Rambam ruled like him; all the more for Tosafot who ruled like R. Shimon, and a kezayit is less than a dried fig as written in Shabbat seif 1 to exclude dried figs etc.; and in Yoma ch. 1 they said the swallowing organ etc.; and in Keritot 14a they said the swallowing organ does not hold more than two olives, and Magen Avraham and Tosafot there s.v. agav — and because of this Tosafot wrote that for eruv we hold like R. Meir, and in the Gemara too etc. "your father acted like whom — like R. Meir" etc. — see there. R. Meir's measure is unknown, for in the Gemara it says there "two loaves" etc. of the Pappa river. It is possible to say per Tosafot's view R. Meir's and R. Yehoshua's measure cited above is twelve eggs — if so dried figs are two-thirds of an egg, and a kezayit which is less than a dried fig is half an egg, and all is fit. But Rambam's view is still wondrous, for he wrote explicitly that a dried fig is a third of an egg as explained; it appears what Rambam ruled six eggs which are eighteen dried figs as we say in the Gemara there is with shells, and a dried fig for him is a third of an egg with shell; and what is written in Yoma there the swallowing organ etc. more than an egg etc. is without shell, as written there in Eruvin "like it without its shell," and on this they said an olive is half an egg, namely without shell, and the measure of one is only that it is not literally half; therefore he ruled for eruv two meals are six eggs — for accordingly a kezayit is less than a third of an egg as explained; and regarding kezayit measure he wrote it is half an egg, namely as explained; and Shulchan Aruch for eruv wrote like Rambam, and for Passover wrote a kezayit is half an egg — and per what is written, Shulchan Aruch's words here are correct both per Tosafot's view according to R. Meir as explained, and per Rambam's view.

chatam-sofer/part-001.txt.1:_: In the Rama gloss "one must compress the hollow" — see Tosafot Yoma ch. 3 mishnah 4 s.v. teme'im etc., and see well in Rambam ch. 4 of Sha'ar Avot HaTumah halacha 13 — see there — that swelling by rain is only d'rabbanan in prohibitions and tumah, and all the more so regarding fulfillment of a mitzvah that is not biblically obligatory.

chok-yaakov/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) That it is like half an egg — so wrote Tosafot Pesachim 108 and in Eruvin ch. Halon — see there; and what Magen Avraham challenged — Tosafot themselves already sensed that difficulty there. And see in Taz ch. 6 of Kelim and at the end of responsum Chut HaShani in the account of calculation, and in Mahariv siman 27, and in Sha'arei Yehuda in his hagahot to Terumat HaDeshen, and see in Beit Hillel on Ohel Moed siman 70.
chok-yaakov/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) And they should eat together — Tur wrote this law briefly in this siman, and what the Acharonim wrote on this is explained above in its simanim each in its place. And he wrote in pesakim of Mahar"i siman 245 that even if one ate the whole plant, namely one stalk with its leaves, he does not fulfill if there is not a kezayit in it, since the plant is deficient in that he does not eat the roots that are fit to eat — end quote.

eliyah-rabbah/part-001.txt.1:_: (א) [Levush] When he comes etc. He prepares silver vessels and gold vessels and silk and brocade garments from all that Hashem graced him, in order to show the joy of his heart in Hashem's kindness.

magen-avraham/part-001.txt.1:_: In Keritot 14a it teaches that a kotevet is two olives, and in siman 472 it teaches that a kotevet is less than an egg; if so a kezayit is slightly less than half an egg, and so per what is written siman 468 seif 3 a dried fig is a third of an egg, and so Rambam; and for a first view it is four-ninths of an egg. And they say in the chapter Hametzui that a dried fig is larger than an olive — see there; if so an olive is at least less than half an egg, only not precisely; and stringently not precisely, but for other matters one must be precise. However it is difficult, for we say in Keritot there the swallowing organ does not hold more than two olives, and everywhere we say the swallowing organ does not hold more than an egg — and it appears to me this means three olives it does not hold; however for Rambam it is difficult that three olives are not like an egg, and one must say that matter in Hametzui deals with a small olive and we require a medium olive, as Maharal wrote siman 496 in the name of Rokeach: compress the hollow. And the same if there is a hollow in matzah it does not combine, per the end of Okatzin.

machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) In Keritot daf 14a — a dried fig is a third of an egg, as he wrote there that the measure of courtyard eruvin for eighteen people or more is eighteen dried figs, which is like six eggs; and for a first view, see siman 468 that eighteen dried figs are eight eggs. And we say in the chapter Hametzui at the beginning of daf 91, and everywhere we say etc. in tractate Yoma daf 80a — and see Tosafot in those places.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) And it appears to me that this is what "three olives" etc. means — that in Keritot it deals with one who considers there is one eating and he is liable for five sin-offerings and one guilt-offering: a tamei who ate chelev like a kotevet (which is two olives) and it is leftover of consecrated things on Yom Kippur, and it challenges why not six sin-offerings as if he added in that eating and ate with it a kezayit of blood. And it answers: it deals with one eating; it does not deal with two eatings. And the Sages measured: the swallowing organ does not hold more than two eggs — end quote of the Gemara; if so the intent is it does not hold three olives, and if one ate a kezayit of blood with a kotevet of chelev it is three olives — see Rashi there. However for Rambam it means he holds a dried fig is a third of an egg as explained; if so three dried figs are like an egg; if so all the more an olive which is smaller than a dried fig — that three olives are smaller than an egg — the difficulties of the Gemara in Keritot are difficult. And in winter days the late R' Israel Heller z"l challenged me on that Gemara in Keritot from the words of Mordechai who brought Magen Avraham above siman 475 s.k. 4 that when crushed it holds three olives — the difficulty of the Gemara in Keritot remains; and I answered him at length — see there in old Tosafot.

mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) That it is like half an egg — medium with its shell; and Rambam's view is a kezayit is a third of an egg — see Magen Avraham and Biur HaGra what they wrote on this. And for practical halacha in a d'oraisa mitzvah such as eating matzah one should be stringent and eat at least like half an egg [unless he is sick and it is hard for him to eat like half an egg, then he may rely on Rambam]. And for maror and the like which are d'rabbanan one may rely b'dieved if he ate like a third of an egg; but l'chatchila, since he must bless on maror, it appears one should not be lenient unless he is a weak person who has difficulty — then he may rely and eat only like a third, and so on. And for Birkat HaMazon whose measure is d'rabbanan in a kezayit [and likewise for Birkat HaMazon] safeik berachot lehakel and he should not bless until he knows he ate like half an egg. And l'chatchila it is fit to beware not to bring himself to safeik berachot and eat like half an egg or much less than a third of an egg in a matter that does not require kezayit [Peri Megadim]. And in my humble opinion it appears fit l'chatchila that he eat like an egg of bread, for otherwise there is concern of a berachah levatalah on the berachah he blessed initially on netilat yadayim per some poskim — and so in siman 488 seif 2 — see there. And now we return to our topic: know that what the Mechaber wrote kezayit like half an egg is not a fixed matter in our time, for some Acharonim proved that eggs found in our time have shrunk greatly, up to half compared to ancient days when the Sages measured; therefore wherever the measure is like half an egg one must measure by an egg in our time. And see in Sha'arei Teshuvah who ruled one should distinguish in measures between a matter whose obligation is from the Torah and a matter whose obligation is d'rabbanan, such as maror nowadays, afikoman, and cups — and it is found that in our time one is obligated to eat matzah up to the measure of an egg, and maror one fulfills b'dieved even if he ate only like a third of an egg, and so on; and see what is written above siman 471 in Biur Halacha s.v. shel revi'it.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) And one should eat it together — see above siman 475 in Mishna Berurah end of s.k. 9.
mishnah-berurah/part-001.txt.1:ג: (ג) And for vegetables one must compress the air space — and the same if there is a hollow in matzah the hollow does not combine toward the measure of kezayit and one must compress it; but if there is no hollow in matzah, even if it is soft and made like a sponge, one need not compress it.

yad-ephraim/part-001.txt.1:_: Taz: and even for the fourth cup we do not require there in siman 472 more than the majority; only here etc. — so it should read.

chokhmat-shlomo/part-001.txt.1:_: Article A. The rate of olives is said to be half an egg. “Here I saw in the Hashem’s Prayer in the Hashem’s Prayer, and the Holy One, in the Flesh, is in the milk that covers the battle which he wrote and that he is not the opposite, and he has written more in his blood and blood. And here it seems that his words do not belong in this is a mistake that is due to the fact that they were not allowed to eat and what they were wrong. And he does not say, 'No.' It is considered eating until you eat much to swallow. It is not a single word written between olives and at least from olives. And yet what is written by Dr. Dalaikin confesses to him if they do not have a go to Moses from Sinai, the Hashem eats in the Bible, and not in the midst of eating it, but not just eating. This is what Hashem’s Word says, “This is what Hashem’s Word is in this time, that it will be written that it will be a lesson that will come in the Hashem’s house in the middle of the earth.” medium. And here I have written in this paragraph of our innovations that are already mentioned that it will be less than an exalted exaltation, and that it will be the same as the olives, and that it is, in fact, that it is the case, that it is not the case, that it is not the same as it is, and that it is not the reason that it is not the cause of the death Thus, the Danin rate does not seem to be as visible as the olive rate and if it were planted between large and medium olives, it is considered a complete error and a sacrifice bar, it is as a result of its intention and mercenary and meticulous. And here is the Hashem’s Prayer in the Holy Spirit and in His presence, and in the midst of the Hashem’s Prayer, all this verse is written, and so on, and in the midst of the Holy Spirit, and in the midst of the Hashem’s Prayer, the Hashem’s Prayer is given to me if he is a great olive or a medium, and he is a blessing If she and her husband are not like her or her husband, and if so, she is not like her or her father’s wife, and if you do not want to do so, he will be able to do so, and if you do not want to do so, then you will be able to do so This is the story of Hashem’s Word, and the Holy Spirit is the same as Hashem’s people. And here is the Hashem’s Prayer, in the midst of Hashem’s Word, that Hashem’s promise is not to drink wine all day, but one of them said to him, “Do not drink any one.” And then, Hashem’s people, and Hashem’s mercy, and Hashem’s promise to Hashem’s people, that they should not be given to them This will require some of the words of no one notice. And what is the case of Hashem’s people, and what is Hashem’s Word, and His Word is written in His words to Moses and why He did not write in His judgments. And he said to him, “Don’t give him a chance to see him and his father’s wife, and to him, if he has given him a lot, it is possible that the second one will be able to see him as the first one, and he will certainly be the fourth of them. And that's what Deiros looks like The blaze of the blaze holds the fourth grade, and it is forgotten that it is held in the fourth grade, and that it is the case that it will be forgotten that it will be a drinker of wine, and that it will be proven to the fourth place. It is also proven in the mountains that the sweat house holds more than olives and that it is not forgotten that it will commit a second-float to the first notice For this reason, the Rambam and my friends, and the Sages and the Sages, saw the connections of Hashem’s Word, and called upon them to make it difficult for Hashem’s people to do so, and to do so with what they do with them

kaf-hachayyim/part-001.txt.1:_: (א) [Seif 1] The measure of a kezayit — some say it is like half an egg. So too Beit Yosef in the name of Tosafot Chullin 103b, and so after Eruvin 83b, and so in Peskei Tosafot Chullin s.v. ervav, and so Mordechai ch. "Ataf" in the Passover order, and so Terumat HaDeshen siman 139 and Pesakim uKhetavim siman 26, and so in derashot Maharil seder Hagadah, and so Mahariw siman 123. That which he wrote this in Shulchan Aruch in the name of "some say" is because this is not agreed, as explained there in Tosafot that some hold a kezayit is less than a third of an egg, and so in Magen Avraham, Peri Chadash, and other Acharonim; Shulchan Aruch adopted half an egg stringently to fulfill according to all. So Knesset HaGedolah seif 1: for halacha one should not be lenient in obligation such as kezayit matzah and maror, or for Birkat HaMazon until he eats specifically half an egg — see there; and Eshel Avraham. Rabbi Zalman seif 1 wrote: for maror which is d'rabbanan, and anything d'rabbanan measured by kezayit, one may rely on those who say slightly less than a third of an egg; but matzah which is d'oraisa and anything d'oraisa — be stringent per the first view; for Birkat HaMazon and Birkat HaMazon whose measure is kezayit — safeik berachot lehakel, do not bless until he ate like half an egg; l'chatchila avoid safeik berachot — eat like half an egg or much less than a third where kezayit is not required; be precise where large measure is leniency and small is stringency, e.g. biur chametz — end quote. That which he wrote for maror d'rabbanan one may rely on lenient — appears for b'dieved if he lacks half an egg or cannot eat more than a third; but for berachah on maror do not bless on less than half an egg — kavod Shabbat safeik berachot lehakel; since many hold kezayit is half an egg, how bless "Who sanctified us" etc.; we wrote above siman 468 seif 46: per Rambam and many poskim egg measure is 18 Egyptian drachma; for eating — kezayit matzah Passover night, maror, Birkat HaMazon — all measured by weight: egg 18 drachma, kezayit half egg nine drachma — see there in many poskim; custom fulfills 18 mitzvot lekhol ha'amim and because of safeik berachot.

peri-megadim/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) The column is written as a pen. In short, Hashem’s word is the light of Hashem’s covenant with Hashem’s Word, and Hashem’s Word is a blessing, and Hashem’s Word is a blessing, and it is a blessing for him, and he will not be given to him If he does not have sufficient water to use this way, Dalai did a derbnan and rejected the prohibition of baptism in the glass of a negotiating meter in the metals of U.S.A.D.C., and it is not possible that he will not be inadvertently. We are accustomed to bringing the bowl and everything that is needed first to be sanctified when the glass is shed or so or on the right will cover the spoon and then the bread of the West will be found on the map. And take a hand of a male lamb into a vengeful arm, and remember to the Passover in if it is possible, and a dish on the ‘laughs’ for celebration, even when it comes to the ‘cold’ takes only a snail They say that they are blessed and snailed when they go to the fire. A. To remove the egg and meat when it is said to be a dazzling as prescribed in some arrangements. Be prepared in the blessing of eating a ray of hay and is therefore not obliged to incite a conversation in the tablet until after Epicoman. All of the feasts of Hashem’s people are in the land of Hashem’s presence, and in the world, Hashem’s presence is in the presence of Hashem’s covenant with Hashem’s people, and Hashem’s mercy is in His hand, and Hashem’s mercy is on him The eating of the groceries will then be made as olives of every complete Hashem, and eats and eats it. "And thou shalt be thrust down to dust, and shalt be thrust down to hell, and shalt not be thrust down to hell." And if he does not have only a blessing, he will be blessed with Hashem’s Word, and if he has a blessing that all will take him, and he will be enslaved, and he will be blessed with him Go out. It will not be sanctified until it was night that we would have seen the stars because there is no doubt that it will be replaced by the T-shirt. It is a great time to make every order before midnight, and it will be eaten from midnight without a blessing. All the sages in the night of A go to the night of a woman do not exclude large people in the fairy tale, even in the night of B, do so in all his or her hands and do not underestimate her. In the column here it means immediately after Epicoman, she will not drink wine in the A.A. and she will not be there. And even after the slicking of the hull between J and D There is no sign that the Hashem will not say, “After Epicoman and David Lane in the banquet that does not receive any compensation from the High Court of Justice.”
